prize_parts.citation: For the development of halide perovskites as solution-processed photovoltaic absorbers and their realization in efficient solid-state solar cells

statement.case_for: Halide perovskites are a structurally simple, solution-processable crystalline family in which composition, dimensionality and defect chemistry can be tuned by design, and within about a decade they reached efficiencies comparable to silicon. The work has reshaped materials and energy chemistry, and the efficiency records have been reproduced independently worldwide. This is the kind of structure-property story, with a whole community adopting a new material class, that I weigh most heavily. The sequence from Miyasaka's sensitizer cells (2009) through Park's solid-state device (2012) to Snaith's mesosuperstructured and planar architectures is traceable and gives a coherent three-person prize.
statement.case_against: Operational stability and lead toxicity are not resolved, and much of the efficiency progress is device engineering rather than a single chemical discovery. Credit is crowded: Gratzel, Kanatzidis and Seok have strong claims, and any trio leaves out major contributors. Kojima does not appear in the credited names, so the configuration has to be built from a contestable list. If the committee judges the field too young in practical deployment, Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling or base editing is the safer, more mature choice.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Buchwald and Hartwig C-N coupling first as a general, overdue bond-forming method, with Kosugi as a possible third name and the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize as a complication.
responses.response: I agree the maturity and industrial adoption are stronger than for perovskites, and I keep it as my first alternative. But the 2010 prize already recognized Pd cross-coupling as a concept, so I think the novelty argument counts more than you suggest, while perovskites open a new materials class. I would not add Kosugi: his tin-amide chemistry was a precursor and not the general, ligand-controlled catalytic method, and a third name would dilute a clean two-person attribution.

responses.point: Linke ranks massively parallel sequencing first and perovskites second, and notes that the three-person limit leaves out Gratzel, Kanatzidis and Seok. He also asks what is new relative to Sanger sequencing (1980).
responses.response: I share your concern about crowded credit and I accept that any trio is contestable. I answer it by tying the citation to the first perovskite-sensitized and solid-state cells (Miyasaka, Park, Snaith), which can be documented. On sequencing, I find the Solexa and 454 lineage dispute harder to resolve than the perovskite credit, and the prize would be read as technology and biology more than chemistry. Your own ranking of perovskites second suggests we do not disagree much on merit.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first as a clean chemical-biology invention with extensive reproduction and early clinical use, a coherent trio of Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, with the Kondo and Nishida priority question flagged but unresolved.
responses.response: I find the invention elegant and I ranked it fourth. My reservation is that CRISPR was recognized in 2020 and that clinical outcomes are still early, so the maturity case is weaker than you state. I also doubt that including trainees is clean, since the Nishida and Kondo parallel cytidine-deaminase work shares priority with Komor and a three-person list would need to settle it. I would support it more if the committee shows the credit is stable.

responses.point: Sparr ranks phase separation first as a general physical-chemical principle for membraneless organization, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the core and Pappu and Mittag left out.
responses.response: The concept is important, but I ask the structural question: for many condensates it is not established that the in-cell assemblies are phase-separated liquids, and the criteria are still disputed. Perovskites have a defined structure, measurable properties and independently confirmed performance. I would want that maturity of evidence before the committee commits, and I am not persuaded that the chemistry framing is stronger than the cell-biology one.

uncertainties: Whether long-term operational stability and lead toxicity make recognition premature
How to split credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis, and whether Kojima's absence from the credited names changes the configuration
Whether the committee will prefer a more mature method (B054) over a materials discovery still in development
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I note only that my own field is electron crystallography of porous materials and that I am a Stockholm University colleague of Peter Brzezinski, which does not bear on any shortlisted candidate.
